I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is what fits my land, my age, and the local weather best. I do not want to take big risks with unfamiliar crops. Wheat and maize have stable demand, I know the field work well, and I can manage them with ordinary machines and hired help when labor is heavy. I will put most of my effort into getting a steady yield instead of chasing the highest possible yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, give moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed for aphids, rust, and weeds. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow hybrid summer maize to catch the season, use a bit more nitrogen because maize responds well, and focus on one good watering if rain is short, plus weed and insect control. I will use ploughing before wheat and rotary tillage before maize because that is the practical way I would manage residue and prepare the seedbed. I am choosing a simple, familiar, lower-risk plan that I believe I can carry through reliably this year.
